- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak unless sentiment is strong.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.2–0.7), model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for lagged periods.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day for 3–5 days.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates mean reversion — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to reflect potential rebound.
